limitations: The alternative explanations remain: another William could be the groom or Bessie’s father; the bride could be another Marion, including the compatible Inveresk Marion-1429/Marione-3049 or Edinburgh Marion-3143 accounts. The earlier 1664 William banns item supplies another adult-couple comparison, not proof of one man’s remarriage. The older William-1087 remains a possible groom comparison if the bride is a different Marion; Marion-3025’s own William-1087 father identification is ungraded and cannot be used circularly to exclude that possibility. William-3974’s recorded 1671 childhood makes him a poor ordinary groom comparison for 1681, without validating the older man’s estimated 1660 birth. Marion’s 11 October/4 November 1655 date discrepancy is retained. Neither a shared surname nor a presumed cousin marriage proves the couple’s ancestry. The pair and maternity share identity premises and are correlated assessments, not independent proofs or mechanically multiplied probabilities. William’s John-3610 father remains 24%; no mother is transferred to his later children, no biological father is changed, and all vital fields remain unchanged.
